pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A plant on a windowsill grows towards the window. What is it responding to? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Soil colour
   C. Wind speed
   D. Sound

2. Which sign of life do ALL living things eventually show? (1 mark)
   A. Flowering
   B. Flying
   C. Making seeds
   D. Dying

3. Which of these is a plant that has a thick main root with thin side roots? (1 mark)
   A. Bean plant
   B. Grass
   C. Maize
   D. Wheat

4. What is the main job of leaves? (1 mark)
   A. Holding the plant in the soil
   B. Making seeds
   C. Taking in water from the soil
   D. Making food for the plant

5. Which of these is NOT alive? (1 mark)
   A. A maize plant
   B. A plastic flower
   C. A grass blade
   D. A young mango tree

6. Which of these animals is an amphibian? (1 mark)
   A. Toad
   B. Tortoise
   C. Snake
   D. Goat

7. Which of these is the best question to ask first when you sort an animal into vertebrate or invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Is it big?
   B. Is it dangerous?
   C. Does it have a backbone?
   D. Is it fast?

8. Which of these is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Snake
   B. Goat
   C. Frog
   D. Earthworm

9. A tadpole grows into a frog. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Animals do not grow
   B. Only fish grow
   C. Tadpoles are plants
   D. Animals grow and change

10. Which of these is NOT an animal? (1 mark)
   A. A wooden toy horse
   B. A tilapia
   C. A housefly
   D. A cow

11. What is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with hair
   B. An animal without a backbone
   C. An animal with a backbone
   D. An animal that flies

12. Which of these is a crab? (1 mark)
   A. A vertebrate with fur
   B. A mammal
   C. An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   D. A bird

13. The stomach is described in the lesson as being like (1 mark)
   A. A hard stone
   B. A long ladder
   C. A sharp knife
   D. A stretchy bag

14. Which of these leaves the body through the anus? (1 mark)
   A. Blood
   B. Saliva
   C. Stomach juice
   D. Faeces

15. Which of these helps prevent germs entering the food? (1 mark)
   A. Covering food
   B. Putting food on the floor
   C. Leaving food open
   D. Letting flies land on food

16. Where does the digestive tube begin? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Stomach
   C. Anus
   D. Small intestine

17. Which of these helps to keep teeth healthy? (1 mark)
   A. Eating many sweets
   B. Biting hard objects
   C. Never visiting a dentist
   D. Brushing twice a day

18. Which of these parts is found before the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Gullet
   C. Large intestine
   D. Small intestine

19. What is digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   B. Throwing away food
   C. Making food hot
   D. Storing food in the stomach for years

20. Which part of the digestive system is long and coiled? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Gullet
   C. Small intestine
   D. Mouth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe the function of each of these parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, flowers. (4 marks)

22. Describe the function of each part of the digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. (5 marks)

23. Draw and label a plant showing roots, stem, leaves and flower. (4 marks)

24. Explain how fibre helps the digestive system. (3 marks)

25. Explain why plants are called living things. (3 marks)

26. Name two invertebrates that are found near your school. (2 marks)

27. Write three safety rules when observing animals in the school compound. (3 marks)

28. Give three ways of caring for animals. (3 marks)

29. Give three examples of how plants respond to changes around them. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Light
   Plants bend and grow towards light coming from one side.

2. D — Dying
   Every living thing dies one day, but not all fly, flower or make seeds.

3. A — Bean plant
   A bean plant has a main root with side roots. Maize and grass have many thin roots.

4. D — Making food for the plant
   Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food.

5. B — A plastic flower
   A plastic flower is made by people and does not grow, respond or reproduce.

6. A — Toad
   Toads have moist skin and start life in water.

7. C — Does it have a backbone?
   The backbone decides the group.

8. D — Earthworm
   An earthworm has a soft body and no backbone.

9. D — Animals grow and change
   Young animals grow and may change shape as they become adults.

10. A — A wooden toy horse
   A toy is not alive. It does not feed, grow or reproduce.

11. B — An animal without a backbone
   Invertebrates have no backbone.

12. C — An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   A crab has no backbone and has a hard shell outside.

13. D — A stretchy bag
   The stomach is a stretchy bag that churns food.

14. D — Faeces
   Faeces leave the body through the anus.

15. A — Covering food
   Covering food keeps out flies and dirt.

16. A — Mouth
   Food enters the body through the mouth.

17. D — Brushing twice a day
   Brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

18. B — Gullet
   Food passes through the gullet before it reaches the stomach.

19. A — Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   Digestion breaks food into tiny parts that can pass into the blood.

20. C — Small intestine
   The small intestine is a very long coiled tube.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water. The stem supports the plant and carries water and food. Leaves make food. Flowers make fruits and seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Mouth: chews and adds saliva. Gullet: pushes food down. Stomach: churns with juices. Small intestine: finishes digestion and absorbs food. Large intestine: takes back water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with four correctly labelled parts: roots below the ground, stem upright, leaves on the stem and a flower at the top.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correctly drawn and labelled part.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fibre in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food and waste move through the intestines and helps prevent constipation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming fibre foods, 1 mark for movement, 1 mark for constipation.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show signs of life. They grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes and die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying they show signs of life and 2 marks for correct signs given.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two correct examples such as ant, earthworm, snail, butterfly, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct invertebrate.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not pick up animals you do not know, do not harm animals, wash hands after touching soil or animals, return animals to where they were found.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide shelter, keep their homes clean, treat sick animals, do not beat them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Growing towards light, roots growing down, touch-me-not folding leaves, flowers opening in the day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.
